record.paper_title: Open questions and perspectives for hadron electromagnetic form factors in space-like and time-like regions.
record.context_brief: Observable signatures of the reaction mechanism
record.original_question: Which experimentally measurable cross sections, polarization components, spin asymmetries, or electron-versus-positron comparisons can identify whether a hadron electromagnetic form-factor measurement is governed by one-photon exchange, two-photon exchange, or their interference?

evidence.quote: • which are the experiments or the observables which sign the reaction mechanism?
One can conclude that the linearity of the Rosenbluth fit is destroyed by the presence of the two photon mechanism.

The experiment, planned at Novosibirk, is a precise measurement of the difference of electron positron elastic scattering on the proton, which is due only to the 2γ contribution, while the sum contains only 1γ terms (neglecting 2γ terms squared [35].

artifact.category_tag: Hadron electromagnetic form factors and two-photon exchange
artifact.status_search_result: The catalogue of observables sensitive to two-photon exchange is well established theoretically: nonlinearity of the Rosenbluth plot, the e^+ p / e^- p cross-section ratio (charge-odd), normal single-spin asymmetries (T-odd), deviations of the polarization-transfer ratio P_T/P_L from the Born value, and forward–backward asymmetries in time-like e^+e^- ↔ p\bar p. Dedicated experiments (VEPP-3 Novosibirsk, CLAS at JLab, OLYMPUS at DESY, and BESIII in the time-like region) have measured several of these and confirm the qualitative picture, with BESIII recently reporting a significant angular asymmetry attributed to 2γ exchange. However, the quantitative resolution of the Rosenbluth-vs-polarization form-factor discrepancy and a complete extraction of 2γ amplitudes remain active research, so the broader physics program is only partially solved.

status_evidence.title: Review of two-photon exchange in electron scattering
status_evidence.snippet: Comprehensive review of observables sensitive to TPE: Rosenbluth nonlinearity, e+/e- ratio, polarization observables, single-spin asymmetries.
status_evidence.claim: Standard list of TPE signatures is established and reviewed.

status_evidence.title: The two-photon exchange experiment at DESY (OLYMPUS)
status_evidence.snippet: OLYMPUS measured e+p/e-p ratio to isolate TPE contributions.
status_evidence.claim: Charge-odd e+/e- comparison is an experimentally realized TPE diagnostic.

status_evidence.title: Exploration of Two-Photon Exchange in proton Form Factors at BESIII
status_evidence.snippet: BESIII observed for the first time a significant angular asymmetry in proton production attributed to TPE.
status_evidence.claim: Time-like forward–backward asymmetry confirmed as a TPE signature.

status_evidence.title: Form Factors and Two-Photon Exchange in High-Energy Elastic e-p Scattering
status_evidence.snippet: Discrepancy between Rosenbluth and polarization-transfer extractions of G_E/G_M attributed to hard TPE, extended to Q^2=8 GeV^2.
status_evidence.claim: Polarization-transfer vs Rosenbluth discrepancy remains an open quantitative issue.
